_comment: world_snapshot_dispositions.json -- the HAND-AUTHORED half of LIB-WORLD's accounting.
tools/gen_world_snapshot.py DERIVES the population (the whole region registry -- bind_stock()
answers for every rid, so `every bound region` is mechanical rather than editorial) and derives
the verdict: a region with a measured extent is CARRIED. This file is where an exclusion would
have to be argued for, and the generator refuses one that is missing, empty, of an undefined
class, stale, doubled onto a zero-extent region, or -- at any price -- one that hides a region
backing a determinism-hash slice.
`exclusion_classes` AND `regions` ARE EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.
LIB-BOOT's population was the write closure of the cfg cluster, where a reader rule decided what
outlived the parse and 84 regions were legitimately excluded across 9 classes. This item's
population is a MEMORY IMAGE at an instant, and there is no equivalent rule to get wrong: the
cheap error is carrying 4 KB nobody reads, and the expensive error is dropping a region the
replay turns out to need -- docs/dead-ends.md G168 is exactly that failure (`Stones` was invisible
to a derivation that had no entry for it, and only a second independent enumeration found it).
So carry is the default, the blob is 827 blocks, and the only derived exclusion is
`exclude:no-extent`: 16 regions whose measured extent is 0, which have no byte to carry at all.
The classes machinery stays because the day an exclusion IS earned it must arrive with a class and
a why rather than as a quiet deletion -- and --selftest injects its own class so the refusals are
watched to fire even while nothing is excluded.
`re_derive` IS THE REAL CONTENT OF THIS FILE. It is the step-0 state a bound-region dump
structurally CANNOT carry, with the evidence for each, so the fixture's completeness claim is
bounded rather than implied. Each entry is an obligation on the IMPORTING host, and LIB-REF's
standalone replay is what enforces it -- a host that skips one reads a stock .bss address or an
unbound mask and diverges loudly at step 0, which is the right failure mode.

menu-ui.why: Menu/lobby-screen state the sim never reads and the importing host rebuilds from its own discovery before any step runs. Carrying it would only cost bytes -- EXCEPT that the block table is the fixture schema: a region that gains a measured extent after the fixtures were recorded turns every recorded world blob into ERR_SCHEMA (-3), which is a re-capture session, not a lint fix. So a menu-only region that becomes carryable late is excluded here with its reason rather than silently re-cutting the fixtures.

BROWSER_UI_ROWS.why: The session browser's row table (llm_lobby_browser_row[1024], mp:R2b, 2026-09-21): written by the browser refresh / the DLL's build_browser_from_store and read only by the browser and llm_lobby_join_head, all before Start. Its extent (8192) entered the addr manifest on 2026-09-21 -- after libref-replay-v1 / libref-*-aisoak-v1 were recorded against the 829-block table -- and the first gate after it refused all three fixtures with rc=-3 (2026-09-22). Not hash-backed; the joiner's browser rows are meaningless to a replaying host.

general.{width_mask,height_mask,big_widt.why: The torus masks. DERIVED from the width/height globals by llm_map_setup_dimensions @0x004989c2, a body libmh already owns translated and shadow-armed (sim/libtrans/sim_lt_map_setup_dimensions.cpp) and already re-invokes on the load path (save/save_live.cpp:466). The blob carries `width` and `height` (RID_WIDTH / RID_HEIGHT) and the host re-derives the rest -- carrying them instead would make the fixture the authority on a value libmh computes, which is the drift shape a single derivation exists to prevent.

pathfinder_params->width_mask.why: PHYSICALLY UNCARRIABLE, not merely undesirable: its storage is a malloc'd 0x20-byte block reached through general.pathfinder_params (+0xc), heap and not a bound region, so a step-0 region dump cannot reach it no matter what the schema says. CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-11 at the exact offset: two step-0 captures from independent launches of the same scenario differ in `general` at +28 and nowhere else (0D8A0030 vs 0C660030 -- two heap addresses), so the POINTER is carried and the block it points at is not. ---- CORRECTED 2026-09-11 (LIB-REF): THIS ROW USED TO SAY THE FIELD WAS 'Re-derived by the same llm_map_setup_dimensions call as the torus masks', FULL STOP. That was half an obligation and the missing half was load-bearing. The field cannot be re-derived until THE BLOCK IT LIVES IN HAS BEEN RE-CREATED: llm_map_setup_dimensions' last store is general.pathfinder_params->width_mask, so on an import path where nothing re-stamps the pointer it WRITES ONE BYTE THROUGH THE RECORDING PROCESS'S HEAP ADDRESS. Measured on the standalone reference host: --steps 1 failed 3 of 30 and 6 of 100 runs, each failure corrupting exactly ONE inactive-player PLAYER_DATA slice and a DIFFERENT one per run, with occasional 0xC0000005. The arithmetic closes it exactly -- carried pointer 0x039A0FD8 plus offsetof(mh_llm_strat_pathfinder_params, width_mask) == 0x16 gives 0x039A0FEE, byte for byte the address the faulting runs reported writing -- and the run-to-run variation is the arena base moving under ASLR: when the stale address happens to land inside the host's arena the write lands silently in whichever bound region covers that offset, and when it does not, the process faults. Invisible to every hash-based oracle because `general` is MF_VIEW. THE COMPLETE OBLIGATION IS TWO CALLS, IN ORDER: llm_strat_pathfinder_init @0x004614f9 (boot stage 4) FIRST, which allocates the 0x20-byte params block and the 0x82480-byte workbuf through the game's own allocator, stores both into `general`, zero-fills the workbuf, refills the 100 STRAT_PATH_JOB_RESULT_TABLE path_steps buffers and re-wires params->{passable,workbuf,job_result_table} to the importing process's bound addresses; THEN llm_map_setup_dimensions. Note this also re-dispositions `general`'s OTHER carried heap pointer, pathfinder_workbuf (+0x1c), which had no row of its own. Landed in state/spine.cpp's re-derive sequence; 120 of 120 consecutive step-1 runs exact afterwards.
pathfinder_params->width_mask.source: tools/data/libmh_call_ledger.json cfg_ReadMapFile DEFER-BLOB contract, plus the two-capture diff; the correction measured 2026-09-11 by bisecting the standalone host's re-derive block (map_setup_dimensions alone reproduced the flake 5 of 100 runs; the zeroing step alone was 100 of 100 clean) and closed by the pointer-plus-offset arithmetic against the observed fault address

the nav-region decomposition (MAP_REGION.why: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-11 BY MEASUREMENT -- THIS ROW'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, AND BOTH HALVES OF IT WERE. It said the importing host must REBUILD the decomposition from the carried `passable` plane, and that LIB-REF's replay would catch any problem loudly ('a wild read, not a drift'). LIB-REF ran it. Neither held. (1) THE REBUILD IS NOT THE RECORDING'S DECOMPOSITION. Measured: canonicalising both grids to tile -> label (so raw pointers do not matter) and comparing, the recording and a fresh llm_map_build_regions over the SAME carried `passable` agree on the region COUNT (180 each) and disagree on 2181 of 65536 tiles -- 3.328% -- with the rebuild leaving 10 more tiles unclaimed (6526 vs 6516 null). The reason is structural rather than a bug in either: the step-0 decomposition is build_regions' output THEN MUTATED by everything that happens before the first sim step -- landing, spawn_ai_base, and building placement through bldg_footprint_set_passable / map_region_split / merge_small_regions. Rebuilding reproduces 'what the builder makes of this plane', never 'what incremental maintenance made of its history'. (2) IT DRIFTS, IT DOES NOT FAULT. The wild-read prediction had the right CLASS and the wrong SYMPTOM: a rebuild produces a structurally valid graph, so nothing dereferences a foreign pointer and nothing crashes -- the standalone replay simply pathfinds differently. Measured: steps 1-289 bit-identical, then at step 290 the AI's unit (player 1, unit 1) sits in unit_state_hover_engage with an allocated path slot where the recording has it in unit_state_deploy_to_building with none (14 bytes in one unit record), plus one extra strategic RNG draw downstream of the different code path. THE FIX (conductor ruling 2026-09-11): the decomposition is CARRIED, not rebuilt -- a derived block of tile -> POOL-SLOT INDEX plus the per-slot region records and the pool bookkeeping, with the host reconstructing the pointer graph from indices. FULL FIDELITY rather than an equivalent partition, because the replay itself runs region_split/merge when buildings are placed, so the POOL must be in the recording's state at step 0; allocation order downstream of a differing free list is the next drift class. build_regions then does NOT run at import -- running it would clobber the carried truth. Design: session_reports/2026-09-11-1430-lib-ref-nav-partition.md. ---- LANDED 2026-09-11, AND MEASURED, INCLUDING THE PART THAT DID NOT WORK ---- The carry is implemented as the world blob's MHNV NAV TRAILER (state/nav_trailer.h; world::FORMAT 1 -> 2, which moves the schema fingerprint so every schema-1 blob is refused -- with rc=-2 ERR_MAGIC, not the -3 ERR_SCHEMA this file's neighbours might lead you to expect, because the format check fires before the schema check). It sits AFTER the last block payload rather than in WORLD_SNAPSHOT_BLOCKS, so worldtest's per-block arms B and C stay unambiguous and gen_world_snapshot's accounting still reports UNACCOUNTED 0. The game's own index-based serialization, llm_map_load_regions @0x00424a68, was read first and used as the FIDELITY CHECKLIST rather than as the format -- with two deliberate departures it justifies: the loader DISCARDS the free list (POOL_FREE_HEAD = 0, never repopulated), which is sound for a game that only loads at a session boundary and NOT for a replay that resumes mid-session and then runs region_split/merge as buildings are placed, so the free list and its ORDER are carried; and `prev` (+0x41c) is NOT carried, because the list is singly linked and prev is dead -- three writers with mutually inconsistent values, and llm_map_save_regions @0x00424773 repurposes it as a seen-flag leaving 1 in every region, so carrying it would make a capture REFUSE after any save. RESULT, measured against the third recording: SLOT-EXACT. 419 pool nodes (180 active / 239 free), both list ORDERS identical by region index, BY_INDEX identical, and 0 of 65536 tiles disagreeing where the rebuild disagreed on 2181. ---- AND THE HONEST NEGATIVE, WHICH THIS ROW OWES ITS OWN EARLIER CONFIDENCE ---- Eliminating the partition difference DID NOT MOVE THE REPLAY: the divergence is still at step 290, still rng_state + units, still 4711 mismatches, 3 of 3 runs. The comparison is controlled rather than impressionistic -- the third recording reproduced the previous one byte-for-byte in orders, clock and both hash streams, so the target is literally the same bytes. So the step-290 attribution recorded above was CORRELATION PRESENTED AS MECHANISM: the 3.328% tile disagreement was real, is now gone, and was not what diverged the replay. The cause remains open and is being hunted; whatever it is, it is unhashed state read at step 290 while every hashed input at 289 matches. Two real defects WERE closed by this work and are the reason to keep it: the partition itself, and -- found only because the partition beside it became exact -- MAP_REGION_GRID's terrain_flags, which zero_foreign_pointer_regions was clearing wholesale because the cell is 8 bytes {region*; terrain_flags} and only the first dword is foreign. That one PREDATES schema 2: build_regions writes the region half only, so the standalone had been replaying with an all-zero obstacle-proximity plane (59020 assigned cells at 0 against a carried distribution of 30878/11715/9292) invisibly, the grid being MF_VIEW. ---- THE ORIGINAL ROW FOLLOWS, kept because its measurement of WHY the raw bytes cannot be carried is still correct and is exactly what the index form exists to work around ---- A CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM'S OWN RECORDED CARRY LIST, and it is a measurement rather than a reading. The tracker text says the blob carries `passable (+ its llm_map_build_regions decomposition)`. The passable PLANE is carried and is fine. THE DECOMPOSITION IS A HEAP-POINTER GRAPH and cannot be: diffing two step-0 captures from independent launches of the same scenario, 23 of 829 blocks differ and MAP_REGION_GRID accounts for 178,851 of the 180,526 differing bytes -- every differing dword a heap address (0F318890 vs 0F3D24D0 at +0, repeated per tile), with MAP_REGION_BY_INDEX (552 B) and the two pool heads differing the same way. So the grid's 256x256 entries point at nodes a malloc gave this process and no other. THE IMPORTING HOST MUST REBUILD IT from the carried `passable` plane -- llm_map_build_regions, the same body map_ReadMap calls -- exactly as it re-derives the torus masks, and for exactly the same reason. Carrying the bytes is not wrong so much as inert: they import cleanly, hash identically, and dereference into another process's heap. LIB-REF's replay is the enforcement, and it will fail loudly rather than subtly (a wild read, not a drift).
the nav-region decomposition (MAP_REGION.source: measured 2026-09-11 three times: the two-capture block diff (why raw pointers cannot be carried); the 3.328% tile-label disagreement between the recording's carried grid and a rebuild from the same passable plane; and, after the trailer landed, the SLOT-EXACT verification of the rebuilt pool against the blob's own trailer and carried grid (libref_host --nav-report, which names regions by carried index and includes both list orders -- a raw --dump-rid cannot do this comparison at all, since the two pools live in different processes and two dumps from two runs of the host differ from each other too). The same run is the evidence for the negative: step 290 unmoved.

STRAT_PATH_JOB_RESULT_TABLE.why: 100 heap pointers, by the same two-capture measurement (398 differing bytes, every differing dword in the 0x0A-0x0F heap range). Path-job results outlive nothing across processes; the host starts with an empty table rather than an imported one. Recorded here so the fixture's completeness claim does not quietly include it.

the host-owned handles and surfaces (HWN.why: Window handles, DirectInput/DirectDraw objects, an open FILE* and pointers into heap sprite storage -- all differ between the two captures and all belong to whatever process is running. None is hashed. A headless standalone replay reads none of them; a host that renders owns them itself. They are carried because carrying is the default and an exclusion is a blindness, NOT because they mean anything after import.

the host-volatile clock samples (GAME_CL.why: GetTickCount-derived samples, and they differ between the two captures exactly as they must. Carried on purpose -- an importing process needs the RECORDING's epoch to interpret the recording's timestamps, which is the one thing it cannot compute for itself -- but none of them may enter a hash or save comparison set, on GAME_CLOCK_RAW_TICKS' standing rule. INPUT_TIME_EPOCH was added to the registry by this item precisely so it could be carried; its appearing in this differing set is the confirmation of its own note, not a surprise.

the 11 baked pointers INTO bound regions.why: The census in every blob header counts dwords whose value EQUALS a bound region's live base; a real step-0 capture reports 11, and they are: G_TEXT_PTRS -> G_TEXT_BLOCK and -> STRAT_SCENARIO_PLANET_NAME_W; TILE_VIS_MAP_PTR @0x00824FF4 -> TILE_VIS_MAP (the tile_objects_ptr class again, this time INSIDE the registry, which is why the G168 sweep over uncovered globals did not surface it); TACT_MOVE_PATH_QUEUE_CUR -> TACT_MOVE_PATH_QUEUE_B; and seven UI widget-list heads. Each is a value the importing host must re-stamp from live_base() after bind, because each is an address rather than a fact. The census is what keeps this list from being something somebody has to remember to look for -- it is recomputed and printed by every capture.
the 11 baked pointers INTO bound regions.source: the capture's own pointer census, cross-read offline against the registry (2026-09-11)

the resolved TLO index.why: Not a region at all since LIFT-TABLE S3: the index crosses host-side inside LIBMH_EVK_INV_PLANET_GFX_SETUP. The blob carries the tileset NAME (current_map_data.tlo_name at +0x11c, and Planets[].tlo_file at +0x20e which IS hashed); resolving the name to an index is libmh's own body calling cfg_GetTloIndex (sim/libtrans/sim_lt_cfg_planet.cpp:113) over LIB-BOOT's imported registry.

tile_objects_ptr @0x005d0ad0.why: A LINK-TIME-BAKED POINTER INTO A BOUND REGION, and the measurement is the point: the 4 bytes at 0x005d0ad0 in DGROUP read 0x00d1ec80, which is exactly REGIONS[RID_TILE_OBJECTS].base. The state matrix records ZERO writers for it in the whole image -- it is initialised data, never assigned at runtime -- and 9 functions read it (llm_strat_minimap_render, map_fow_UpdateFoWPlus_impl, llm_strat_fow_remove_sight_apply, four tactical tile walkers, ...). It is not a registry region, so no bound-region dump contains it, and it is WRONG the instant a host binds tile_objects anywhere but its stock .bss. The importing host must stamp it from live_base(RID_TILE_OBJECTS) after bind. Found by LIB-WORLD's G168 cross-check (2026-09-11): one of 297 globals the sim closure touches that no registry region covers.
tile_objects_ptr @0x005d0ad0.source: measured against the image bytes of /eng/mh.exe (DGROUP raw), plus tmp/state_matrix.json accessor cells

fow_ptr @0x005202c0.why: The same shape and the same measurement: the dword reads 0x00794fa0 = REGIONS[RID_FOG_OF_WAR].base, zero writers anywhere in the image, read by map_fow_UpdateFoWPlus_impl (x2) and llm_strat_fow_remove_sight_apply. Same obligation on the host, same enforcement by LIB-REF's replay.
fow_ptr @0x005202c0.source: measured against the image bytes of /eng/mh.exe (DGROUP raw), plus tmp/state_matrix.json accessor cells

_G_LLM_STRAT_MINIMAP_RESOURCE_GRID_PTR @.why: Recorded for completeness rather than as an obligation: the dword reads 0x00c28530 = REGIONS[RID_RESOURCES].base, same baked-pointer class as the two above, but every reader is a renderer (llm_strat_minimap_render and friends) and a headless replay never runs one. A host that DOES render must stamp it the same way. _G_LLM_STRAT_MINIMAP_VIGNETTE_MASK_PTR @0x005d0ad4 and PTR__G_LLM_TLO_SHADE_TABLE_00559a08 are the same class.
_G_LLM_STRAT_MINIMAP_RESOURCE_GRID_PTR @.source: measured against the image bytes of /eng/mh.exe (DGROUP raw)

G_TEXT_PTRS[] (RID_G_TEXT_PTRS, 806 entr.why: THE THIRD MEMBER OF THE BAKED-POINTER CLASS THIS FILE ALREADY NAMES, and the first one a HEADLESS STRATEGIC run reaches. The class was stated as 'the link-time-baked pointers into bound regions (tile_objects_ptr, fow_ptr) which are wrong the moment a host binds the pointee anywhere but its stock .bss ... obligations on the importing host, not gaps'. G_TEXT_PTRS is the localized text pool's index: 806 dwords, MF_VIEW, every live entry pointing INTO G_TEXT_BLOCK at the RECORDING process's address. WHY IT WAS NEVER ENUMERATED, and this is the generalisable part: the blob's own census counts `region_head_ptrs` = dwords whose value EQUALS some carried region's live base. These point at 720 different INTERIOR offsets, so the census could never have seen one -- interior pointers are structurally invisible to a base-equality count, and the eleven it does report are a different population entirely. A capture-side census is therefore a LOWER BOUND on this class, not an enumeration of it. WHY NO REPLAY EVER HIT IT: the text pool is read when the sim FORMATS a message (building completion, advisor notices, damage reports), and every replay fixture runs with replay_suppress_enqueue=1, which generates none. LIB-REF-LIVE's live loop generates them. MEASURED 2026-09-11 on libref-live-aisoak-v1: steps 1..2000 bit-identical, then step 2001 faulted 0xC0000005 in mh::crt::detail::format_core<wchar_t> reading 0x0058696C -- byte for byte one of the carried entries, confirmed by dumping RID_G_TEXT_PTRS from the standalone at step 1 (720 entries inside the stock G_TEXT_BLOCK span, 85 at the .rdata constant 0x0050108F, 1 at STRAT_SCENARIO_PLANET_NAME_W, 0 zero).
G_TEXT_PTRS[] (RID_G_TEXT_PTRS, 806 entr.obligation: THE IMPORTING HOST RE-STAMPS THE TABLE, immediately after libmh_import_world and before the first hash. Four outcomes per entry and NO FIFTH -- anything unrecognised REFUSES the import and names the entry (B6.4: never silently shrink): (i) inside some carried region's ORIGINAL span -> rebase onto that region's live binding; (ii) an adjudicated .rdata constant -> point at a HOST COPY OF THE REAL BYTES, read out of the frozen EN image at generation time and baked into the generated table, so the pool's default is faithful rather than invented if it ever reaches hashed state; (iii) zero -> keep; (iv) inside two overlapping region spans -> REFUSE, not guessed. THE POINTEE SIDE IS REGISTRY-DRIVEN AND THAT IS A CORRECTION THE INSTRUMENT FORCED: the first draft adjudicated only 'inside G_TEXT_BLOCK' and its refusal immediately named entry 0xa8 = 0x00E589C0, the scenario-planet UTF-16 scratch buffer STRAT_SCENARIO_PLANET_NAME_W (rid 758, offset +0) that llm_strat_scenario_planet_clone publishes there. A carried text pointer may name ANY bound region.
G_TEXT_PTRS[] (RID_G_TEXT_PTRS, 806 entr.implementation: src/mh_dll/libref_host/main.cpp restamp_text_ptrs(), over the generated host-only table src/mh_dll/libref_host/host_stock_bases.gen.h (tools/gen_libref_stock_bases.py). The table carries mh.exe's per-region bases and is HOST-ONLY by construction: the header #errors without MH_LIBREF_HOST_TU, and tools/lint_libmh_layering.py fails if any file under src/mh_dll/mh/ so much as names it (mutation-proven both on inline fixtures and by planting the include in a real module TU). LIBMH'S ZERO-VA GUARANTEE IS UNTOUCHED AND ITS SCOPE IS UNCHANGED: LIB-REF-SPLIT S5 protects the libmh ARTIFACT, enforced by scan_libmh_vas.py over libmh.lib, and this table is compiled into the host exe only. An importer knowing the recording's layout is a relocation reader's job, not a module dependency (conductor ruling, 2026-09-11).
G_TEXT_PTRS[] (RID_G_TEXT_PTRS, 806 entr.red_arm: libref_host --no-restamp-text-ptrs. MEASURED both directions on libref-live-aisoak-v1: with the re-stamp off the 2001 fault reproduces; with it on the run completes 5000/5000 ALL STEPS IDENTICAL, 0 traps, 0 refusals, 0 unadjudicated entries (721 rebased into 2 carried regions, 85 to the host .rdata copy). The anti-vacuity guard is part of it: a re-stamp that rebased NOTHING fails loudly, because a fixup that touched nothing and reported success is exactly what this bug looked like from every replay.
G_TEXT_PTRS[] (RID_G_TEXT_PTRS, 806 entr.residue: A PER-REGION ADJUDICATION PASS IS OWED. A screen over all 829 blocks of the live blob found 41 holder regions containing 4913 dwords that land inside some carried region's stock span. Most are expected aliasing -- G_TEXT_BLOCK (2482) and SPRITE_PIX_OFFSETS (1071) hold text and pixel bytes, where a 4-byte value landing in a 300 KB span is noise. Only G_TEXT_PTRS has the DENSITY signature of a pointer table: 721 of its 806 dwords, 89%, all into one region. The other 40 holders are unadjudicated and are NOT claimed to be pointers here. The live replay is itself the enforcement instrument for any that are real: now that every region lives in its own arena binding, a wrong pointer either faults (loud) or moves a hashed region (caught).
